title: Uncovering the Hidden Cost of Model Compression
review_status: full-text audit complete; eight image datasets, ResNet/CLIP/DeiT/Swin checkpoints, visual-prompting protocols, sparse/quantized transfer, data budgets, calibration results and scope checked
sections_checked: Experimental setup: eight datasets, model families, three seeds and >15,000 runs
Sparse ResNet transfer and compressed CLIP results
Quantized DeiT/Swin and cross-modal reprogramming tables
venue_year_verified: arXiv v3 dated 2024-03-15; first submitted 2023-08-29; sample stratum follows arXiv first-submission year
evidence_note: Sparse checkpoints usually underperform dense ones under visual prompting, with dataset- and data-budget-dependent gaps (e.g. about 45 percentage points for 4x-compressed CLIP on OxfordPets under ILM-VP); some datasets have small gaps. 2-bit quantization also costs accuracy, while calibration trends differ: sparsity tends to worsen ECE, quantization tends to maintain or reduce it. Three seeds; specific vision checkpoints and adaptation protocols.

title: Are Compressed Language Models Less Subgroup Robust?
review_status: full-text audit complete; 18 compression settings, three English datasets, subgroup definitions, worst-group/mean results, method differences and limitations checked; venue chronology corrected
sections_checked: MultiNLI, CivilComments and SCOTUS subgroup setup
Results by dataset, model size, quantization and distillation
venue_year_verified: arXiv v1 submitted 2024-03-26; peer-reviewed EMNLP 2023 (DOI 10.18653/v1/2023.emnlp-main.983); stratification uses arXiv first-submission year
evidence_note: Worst-group results depend on dataset and compression procedure, not size alone. Many CivilComments compressed variants improve WGA despite slightly lower mean accuracy; MultiNLI and SCOTUS more often show declines. Post-training quantization is generally less subgroup-robust than quantization-aware training in this experiment. English/BERT/three datasets; procedures mostly studied in isolation.

title: GraphFM: A Comprehensive Benchmark for Graph Foundation Model
review_status: full-text audit complete; eight methods, six graphs, full/mini-batch procedures, cross-task generalization, alternative stopping criteria, runtime-driven omissions and stated scope checked
sections_checked: Dataset and method inventory; common hyperparameter search
RQ1-RQ4 protocols and five-seed full-batch results
venue_year_verified: arXiv:2406.08310v2; initially submitted 2024-06-12; no peer-reviewed venue identified in reviewed version
evidence_note: Eight graph self-supervised methods across six conventional node-feature graphs. Many checkpoints selected on node classification transfer well across tasks on small graphs; large-graph performance and the effects of mini-batch strategy vary by method/task. Validation on link prediction or clustering can improve that target task, but does not uniformly improve all tasks. Several Reddit comparisons excluded because runs commonly exceeded 24 hours.

title: Understanding the Effect of Model Compression on Social Bias in Large Language Models
review_status: targeted counterexample full text inspected via ACL Anthology primary PDF; quantization/distillation, model families, BiasBench metrics, results and author-stated benchmark limitations checked
sections_checked: Sections 2-3: BiasBench, model families and compression setup
Results: quantization/distillation across gender, race and religion measures; language-model score trade-offs
Section 4: limitations on identity coverage, Western bias framing and preliminary status
evidence_note: Dynamic int8 quantization and distillation reduce several measured bias scores; quantization exhibits a regularizer-like effect with an apparent best LM-score/bias trade-off near 20% of original Pythia pretraining steps. Effects depend on model, category and task. The authors state the measures cover only gender/race/religion, mostly Western stereotypes, and are preliminary/not production-ready.
